findings.evidence: Terminology Notes section (line 49-53) and Program Coordination section (line 64-65) interrupt the procedural flow with mixed-audience jargon and unrelated content.
findings.fix: Move Terminology Notes to an appendix or eliminate it; consolidate Program Coordination into logical preceding sections or remove unrelated content (travel audits, coffee budget).
findings.violation: The document's logical sequence for an employee reader is broken by sections that mix audiences and introduce content (travel audits, remote-work guidance, coffee budget) unrelated to the stipend program.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout.
findings.fix: Rewrite the opening sentence to state the topic the rest of the paragraph covers.
findings.violation: The paragraph's opening sentence shares almost no vocabulary with the rest of the paragraph, so it does not preview the paragraph's actual topic.

findings.evidence: An incomplete request pauses the timeline (line 29). The stipend request moves to final processing (line 21). A separate audit reviewed unrelated travel expenses (line 65).
findings.fix: Replace abstract nouns with the actual actors: 'When a request is incomplete, the processor pauses the timeline.' 'The manager and finance team move the request to final processing.' 'HR conducted a separate audit of travel expenses.'
findings.location: Approval Timeline, How to Apply, Program Coordination
findings.violation: Multiple sentences use abstract nouns (request, audit) as subjects instead of naming the person or role actually performing the action, leaving the reader unclear who is responsible for each step.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter.
findings.fix: Delete all sentences except the first. The section titled 'Program Coordination' should cover only coordination of the stipend program, not tangential HR/operations matters.
findings.violation: A reader who reads only the first and last sentences of this section cannot name a coherent theme. The four sentences pursue four unrelated topics (stipends, audits, remote work, coffee) with no connection, so the section has no coherent meaning.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter.
findings.fix: Delete the three sentences about audits, remote work, and coffee budget. They share no topic with the opening sentence and break the paragraph's cohesion entirely.
findings.violation: Each sentence opens with wholly new information unrelated to the prior sentence. Sentences 2 - 4 shift topic from stipends to audits to remote work to coffee budgets, with no signal connecting any two consecutive sentences.

findings.evidence: You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the covered purchase amount after that monthly review.
findings.fix: Separate instructions for different audiences (employees vs. finance/payroll staff) into distinct sections with clear audience labels.
findings.violation: The section mixes instructions for employees ('you record') with operational steps for finance and payroll, leaving unclear which reader should act on which sentence.

findings.evidence: The benefits team publishes the equipment catalog (line 5), but the IT asset group updates the equipment catalog (line 61). The finance office reviews the reimbursement log (line 69) and Finance reconciles the request log (line 51).
findings.fix: Define once which team owns the catalog; clarify whether 'reimbursement log' and 'request log' are the same document or different steps in one process.
findings.location: Program Overview, Eligibility, Special Cases, Program Coordination, Terminology Notes
findings.violation: The document uses overlapping terms for the same concepts without clear equivalence: two teams update/publish one 'catalog'; 'reimbursement log' and 'request log' are used as if they are different records but their relationship is undefined.

findings.evidence: Employees start a stipend request in the benefits portal. The portal walks through each step in order. Also, the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing. The employee receives a confirmation email once processing finishes. Then, the employee reviews the confirmation summary before submitting the final request.
findings.fix: Reorganize the sequence: (1) start request, (2) employee reviews summary, (3) manager reviews and signs, (4) finance confirms, (5) final processing, (6) confirmation email. State the main sequence before inserting manager/finance steps.
findings.violation: The section presents steps out of logical order: the employee reviews the summary after it has already moved to final processing with manager and finance approval, which reverses the expected review → approval → processing sequence.

findings.evidence: Also, the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing.
findings.fix: Move the interrupting clause elsewhere, or split it into its own sentence.
findings.violation: 3 comma-set-off clause(s) totalling 14 words intervene between the sentence's apparent subject and its verb.

findings.evidence: An incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives. The...
findings.fix: Open the paragraph with a transition word that states its relationship to the prior paragraph.
